definition: A local stand-in for PingOne Authorize. It answers decision requests in the same shape from rules you can edit, so a client can run its normal flow with no tenant. It is a simulation: its verdicts are not PingOne's. The response shapes follow the AI-DEMO2 integration and are UNVERIFIED against PingOne's own documentation.

The editable knobs the Mock engine decides with: the deny limit, the step-up limit, the transaction types that always need consent, the MCP tools that are never allowed and the tools that need a person's approval. Saved rules are a sparse overlay on the defaults; a value set back to its default is dropped.
What the rules said about one request: PERMIT, DENY, or INDETERMINATE (the request had nothing the rules can read). INDETERMINATE is shown as such and is never read as a permit.

The named reasons that come back with a verdict. A gate such as step-up, consent or human approval is a PERMIT plus a statement whose code names it (STEP_UP_MFA, HITL_CONSENT), as PingOne's endpoint signals it (UNVERIFIED).

A client_credentials access token a client gets from the mock token endpoint with the mock worker client id and secret. It is Mock-issued, labelled as such, and only good here. Reset ends every token issued so far.

The token, decisionEndpoints, decision and recentDecisions routes under /pingone, with the environment id in the path accepted as given. A client such as the P1AZ Inspector in Real mode can point at it unchanged. The on-prem PingAuthorize path is also answered. Both shapes are UNVERIFIED against a real PingOne or PingAuthorize.

Puts the session back to a fresh start: rules back to defaults, the decision log cleared, issued tokens ended. The worker credentials are kept, so a client that already holds the secret keeps working.

A guard that refuses every outbound socket, DNS lookup, fetch, UDP send and UDP connect. This app only answers requests; it never calls out. A self-test proves the guard works and a test proves a whole session makes zero attempts.
